chunks: Al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Hamid who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who buys a female slave while she is pregnant, does he have intercourse with her? He said: No. I said: Below the vulva? He said: He does not approach her. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: 'He does not approach her below the vulva' is based on a type of dislike (karahah), not prohibition (haram), as indicated by the preceding narrations, and this indicates it.

key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: Dislike (a legal status less severe than prohibition)
key_terms.يَطَؤُهَا: He has intercourse with her (specifically vaginal)

ai.seo_question: Is it forbidden or just disliked for a master to have intercourse with a pregnant female slave he owns?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfabar highlights the juristic distinction between absolute prohibition (haram) and recommended dislike (karahat al-tanzih) regarding sexual intimacy with a pregnant female slave, a key debate in Shia fiqh. Imam al-Sadiq (as) clarifies that while vaginal intercourse is discouraged, other forms of intimacy are permissible, reflecting a nuanced approach to marital rights within slavery. This ruling underscores the practical application of Quranic principles to the specific legal category of 'ma malakat aymanukum' (those whom your right hands possess).
